frequency_question: How often do paired sovereign principals successfully execute a treaty extension or successor framework before the expiration of a legacy water-sharing pact?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral river treaties expiring or up for renewal involving sovereign states with established joint river commissions; excludes unilateral actions or failed negotiations where no treaty existed prior.

cases.name: US-Canada Columbia River Treaty regime reviews
India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty continuous implementation/modifications
South Africa-Lesotho Highlands Water Project phase agreements
Senegal River Basin Development Organization (OMVS) protocol renewals
Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty water annex implementation

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major transboundary water regime renewals; universally successful historically when foundational institutional frameworks already exist.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unratified technical adjustments between minor basins.
skeleton: 6 historical transboundary water regimes undergoing major renewal or successor processes, sampled across different continents
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 major instances where active treaties reached structural renewal milestones under motivated principals
validity_reason: Norms of international water law and institutional persistence change slowly over multi-decade horizons.
